subject: gk
question: According to the seventh schedule of the Indian Constitution, Agriculture is in which list?
solution:
The correct answer is __**State List**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution divides the powers and functions of the government into three lists: **Union List, State List, and Concurrent List**.
 
• Agriculture is exclusively mentioned under the **State List in Entry 14**.
 
• The State List empowers state governments to make laws and policies regarding agricultural matters, as it is considered a state subject.
 
• Subjects under the State List include land improvement, agricultural education, research, protection of plants, and other agricultural matters.
 
• The Union government has limited interference in agricultural matters unless they overlap with subjects in the Concurrent List or in cases of national importance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Union List:**

 
 
• This list contains subjects of national importance such as defense, foreign affairs, atomic energy, and banking.
 
• Only the Parliament of India can make laws on subjects in the Union List.
 
 
 
• **State List:**
 
 
• This list contains subjects of local or state importance such as police, public health, and agriculture.
 
• State legislatures have exclusive power to legislate on these subjects.
 
 
 
• **Concurrent List:**
 
 
• This list includes subjects where both the Union and State governments can legislate, such as education, forests, and marriage.
 
• In case of conflict, the Union law prevails over the state law.
 
 
 
• **Important Agricultural Initiatives:**
 
 
• Although agriculture is a state subject, national-level schemes like PM-KISAN and Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) are implemented by the Union government.
 
• These schemes aim to provide financial support and insurance to farmers across India.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Agriculture:**
 
 
• Agriculture is a crucial sector in India, employing over 50% of the workforce and contributing around 18% to the GDP.
 
• The decentralization of agricultural policymaking allows states to address region-specific issues effectively.
